Information since October points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, but the persistent inflation shortfall and weak business fixed investment/exports are consistent with New Keynesian evidence that anchored expectations and demand shortfalls can keep inflation below target even with low unemployment (Galí and Gertler 1999; Woodford 2003). The decision to hold the funds rate while using T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves fits the view that liquidity operations can stabilize money markets without materially changing the policy stance (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005; Ang and Piazzesi 2003; Rudebusch and Wu 2008). The ongoing softness in capex also aligns with financial frictions evidence that lower internal funds/net worth depress investment (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994). Overall tone is cautiously positive but tempered by below-target inflation and capex/export weakness.
